transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Priya Natarajan (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (HorizonAI Head of ML), Eva Gomez (Engineering Manager), Liu Chen (NLP Lead)

[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to keep this to 45 minutes to run through scope for the POC and pick a short list of open models that match your latency/quality needs. quick intros?
[00:07] Samir: yeah, hi i'm samir, lead ml at horizon. we're building a multi-lingual customer insights agent for ecomm and healthcare verticals, expect lots of short questions and some longer summarization requests.
[00:18] Eva: eva here, eng manager, i'll be the main contact for infra and we own deployment.
[00:24] Liu: liu, nlp lead, i'll own prompts/quality evals and handle benchmark setup.
[00:28] Marcus: marcus from redwood, i'll scope the runtimes and run the bench sheet with you.
[00:33] Priya: awesome. quick context from our side: goals for the POC are twofold — validate model quality across en/es/pt and medical domain, and hit latency targets under your expected 95th percentile of 450ms for short queries. cost per 1k tokens also matters, aiming to be under $0.40 equivalent for hosted inference in the pilot.
[01:02] Samir: sounds right. a few clarifiers: we have a mix of short Q/A (~85% under 100 tokens) and long summarizations (10% around 800-2k tokens). peak concurrency is small, like 20-30 rps for short queries. we care about hallucination rates on medical intents.
[01:28] Marcus: perfect, that helps. on sizing — if that's your workload shape we usually recommend testing both a medium-size dense model and a quantized LLM variant to measure tradeoffs. for open-models, our initial shortlist is: Llama 2-13B (7B if latency needs cut), Mistral-Instruct variants, and a smaller mosaic/RedPajama 12B q4 variant. we also suggested trying Llama-3-13B if you want to probe quality but it's heavier.
[01:55] Liu: could you repeat the names? there are a lot and our procurement team asked about licensing differences.
[02:01] Priya: sure — so shortlist: Llama 2 13B (open weights, wide adoption), Mistral-Instruct (good instruction tuning), RedPajama 12B q4b (fast quantized path), and optionally Llama 3 13B if you want higher base quality, though that may require Dedicated or more memory.
[02:26] Eva: and how do you see multilingual performance — our Spanish and Portuguese traffic is ~30% of volume and we'd like equitable accuracy.
[02:33] Marcus: multilingual is model-specific — Mistral and Llama variants have decent multi-lingual generalization but tend to drop on Portuguese medical terms. we recommend adding a targeted eval set in your prompt suite focusing on medical Portuguese and Spanish. fine-tuning or LoRA on a small in-domain corpus can move the needle quickly.
[02:54] Samir: fine. success criteria — can we put concrete thresholds? like top-line: 95p latency < 450ms for <100 token queries, avg token cost <= $0.40 per 1k tokens for pilot, and accuracy/hallucination target: for medical NER/QA F1 > 0.78 and hallucination rate < 5% on our audit prompts.
[03:18] Priya: yeah, that's exactly the type of SLO we want for the POC. we'll encode those into the benchmark plan and measure across models.
[03:24] Liu: for hallucination audit — we have a 200-prompt set with ground truth and ambiguous cases. we'll share it but it'll need anonymization.
[03:33] Eva: infra constraints — we currently run on GCP us-central, but for the POC we can accept hosted Redwood endpoints. if we get to Dedicated, we will need VPC peering and KMS integration.
[03:47] Marcus: noted. Hosted will be fastest to get bench data. Dedicated/Private will be next step if you hit scale or there are compliance needs. we do KMS/HSM plus audit logs for private.
[03:59] Samir: one question on caching and prefix reuse — many of our queries share context, can redwood do KV cache reuse across sessions?
[04:07] Marcus: yes our runtime supports prefix/KV cache and we can configure persistent caches per customer. that reduces token cost and latency for repeated contexts, exact gains depend on your prefix hit rate.
[04:20] Priya: okay let's walk through the bench plan. Marcus?
[04:24] Marcus: bench plan high level: 1) we take your anonymized traces and split into short/long buckets, 2) run 3-5 candidate models across identical prompt templates, 3) measure quality (F1/EM/hallucination), latency P50/P95, and token cost per 1k on our hosted profiles, 4) report a ranked table with recommended model + config (batching, quant, cache). We'll supply a spreadsheet; you'll drop traces and the prompt set.
[04:49] Liu: timeline? we need results by mid-July ideally to decide on Q3 rollout.
[04:55] Marcus: doable — proposed timeline: today kick-off and model shortlist (done), by 2026-07-03 Redwood runs initial bench on synthetic subset and shares template, by 2026-07-10 Redwood runs full bench using your traces, report and recommendation by 2026-07-13, follow-up deep-dive on quant/fine-tuning week of 2026-07-13. does that align?
[05:17] Samir: yes that works, we can get traces and the prompt set by 7/6.
[05:23] Eva: legal/infosec — we'll need SOC2 type 2 report and contractual language around data residency. also, does Redwood persist logs by default?
[05:33] Priya: we keep minimal request traces for observability, retention configurable; for POC we can keep short retention and we have a SOC2 report and security whitepaper — i'll send those.
[05:43] Samir: great. any red flags on hallucinations for med domain? which model usually performs best?
[05:48] Marcus: from our experience, Llama 3 variants typically have strongest factuality but are heavier; Mistral-Instruct is strong for instruction following and often competitive on QA after light fine-tuning; quantized RedPajama is fast and cheap but needs more prompt engineering. For medical domain, fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a vetted knowledge base reduces hallucinations significantly. we'd recommend RAG as part of the POC if your KB is available.
[06:20] Liu: we do have a curated KB for treatments and product docs. could we run both a pure LM and RAG variant in the bench?
[06:26] Marcus: yes run both in parallel — we'll add RAG configs to the bench matrix. note: RAG will add latency due to retrieval but reduces hallucination; caching retrievals helps.
[06:36] Priya: on cost estimates — we'll run token-cost calc in the spreadsheet but rough hosted price differentials: Llama-13B dense might be ~2-3x cost of a 7B or quantized 12B; exact price depends on batching and KV hit rate. We'll surface per-1k token cost in the bench table.
[06:58] Samir: fine. for multilingual, should we include a translation step pre/post or native model support?
[07:05] Marcus: native model support is cleaner if model supports the languages natively; if not you can do translate-to-en, run model, then translate back, but that introduces jitter and latency. recommend testing native first.
[07:19] Eva: any infra notes for a hosted POC — do you need keys from us? network access?
[07:24] Priya: for hosted POC we just need the prompt set and traces. for Dedicated we'll need VPC peering details and KMS endpoints later.
[07:34] Liu: can you also show an example of quantization accuracy loss? we want to see where q4b degrades F1 for NER.
[07:40] Marcus: yes that's a standard check — we'll include q8/q4b comparisons in the bench. sometimes NER drops 2-6 points depending on granularity; we'll quantify it in your eval.
[07:52] Samir: any competitor risk? like if we evaluate OpenAI or Anthropic as a high-quality baseline?
[07:58] Priya: we can include closed API baselines as a comparison row in the bench, but note cost/terms differences. many customers do a hybrid: use open models for the bulk and an API fallback for high-criticality queries.
[08:12] Eva: can Redwood host a canary deploy if we move to Dedicated midway?
[08:16] Marcus: yes, canary and A/B partitions are supported. rollbacks and automatic fallback to hosted variants are also built in.
[08:25] Priya: ok i'll recap next steps — priya will send pricing and security docs; marcus will share bench sheet and run synthetic bench by 7/3; horizon will provide traces + prompt set by 7/6; bench results target 7/13; schedule deep-dive week of 7/13. any other items?
[08:44] Samir: nothing else, thanks everyone.
[08:47] Eva: thanks.
[08:48] Liu: thanks, bye.

Action items recap:
- Priya: send SOC2 whitepaper, security one-pager, and POC pricing by 2026-07-02.
- Marcus: share benchmark spreadsheet and run initial synthetic runs by 2026-07-03; include q4b/q8 comparisons and RAG config.
- HorizonAI (Samir/Liu): anonymize and upload 2 weeks of traces + 200 audit prompts by 2026-07-06.
- Eva: confirm legal point of contact and procurement timeline by 2026-07-05.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors observed (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'Redwood Dedicate' for Redwood Dedicated). Speaker labels sometimes overlap and there is light crosstalk.
